title: Walking-groupoid restriction is an equivalence onto invertible components
statement:
Give small simplicial categories the Bergner model structure with generators and path-component categories as in [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting] and [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-cell-stability]. Use the framed Kan homotopy function complexes, ordinary-model homotopy category and natural comparison conventions of [lem-coef-simplicial-derived-pushout-mapping]. Let $[1]$ be the discrete simplicial category on two objects $0,1$ with exactly one nonidentity arrow $0\to1$. Let $\mathbb J$ be the discrete two-object groupoid with exactly one arrow for every ordered pair of objects, and let $i:[1]\to\mathbb J$ send the distinguished arrow to its distinguished isomorphism. For every small simplicial category $T$ and fibrant replacement $T\to RT$, consider
$$r=i^*:\operatorname{Map}^h(\mathbb J,T)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}^h([1],T).$$
The walking arrow is cofibrant, so choose its frame with degree zero $[1]$; vertices of its function complex are actual enriched functors $[1]\to RT$. Let $E_T$ be the union of the connected components of $\operatorname{Map}^h([1],T)$ represented by those functors whose distinguished arrow has an invertible class in $\pi_0(RT)$. Membership in this union is independent of the chosen representative. Restriction factors through $E_T$, and the resulting map $\operatorname{Map}^h(\mathbb J,T)\to E_T$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Equivalently, every homotopy fiber of $r$ over an invertible-arrow vertex is weakly contractible, and its homotopy fiber over a noninvertible-arrow vertex is empty. There are compatible frame and cofibrant-replacement choices for $i$ for which $r$ is a Kan fibration. With these choices its factorization through $E_T$ is a trivial Kan fibration. The factorization and weak equivalence are natural in $T$ up to the homotopies supplied by the function-complex comparisons. No strict inverse data in $RT$ and no saturation hypothesis are required.

source.place: HTT Notation A.3.5.1, Remark A.3.5.2 and Lemma A.3.5.3, with the simplicial-set invertibility hypothesis in Example A.3.2.18. The full function-complex assertion is an agent-stated strengthening of the pointwise extension criterion, not the pi_0 assertion of Proposition A.3.5.5. Read online 2026-10-17; archival HTT WANTED. No Stacks tag states it.

proof.text: Put $A=[1]$. It is cofibrant: first attach its two objects using $\varnothing\to\{0\}$, then its single arrow using $U(\partial\Delta^0)\to U(\Delta^0)$. In the Bergner model structure factor $i$ as a cofibration $j:A\to E$ followed by a trivial fibration $q:E\to\mathbb J$. Thus $E$ is cofibrant and $q$ is a cofibrant replacement of $\mathbb J$ compatible with $i$. The equivalence $\pi_0E\to\pi_0\mathbb J$ reflects isomorphisms, so $j(a)$ is invertible in $\pi_0E$. This uses invertibility of a class, not a strictly chosen inverse in $E$.

source.place: Notation A.3.5.1; elementary generator and model-factorization argument.

proof.text: Construct compatible frames with prescribed degree zero. Give the arrow category of $\mathrm{sCat}$ the direct Reedy structure on $0\to1$. Its cofibrant objects are precisely cofibrations with cofibrant source, so $j$ is cofibrant. In its cosimplicial Reedy model category factor the initial-object map to $\operatorname{const}(j)$ as a cofibration followed by a trivial fibration, keeping its degree-zero factorization equal to $\varnothing\to j\xrightarrow{1}j$. The degree-by-degree extension clause of the Reedy theorem permits this prescription. Write the resulting arrow of frames as $A^\bullet\to E^\bullet$, with $A^0=A$, $E^0=E$. Both augmentations are objectwise weak equivalences, and the relative latching conditions are $L_nA^\bullet\to A^n$ and $A^n\amalg_{L_nA^\bullet}L_nE^\bullet\to E^n$ being cofibrations. These are therefore frames in the sense of the derived-pushout node.

source.place: Agent construction by the Reedy factorization and prescribed-degree-zero clauses of lem-coef-reedy-model-structure; cf. cosimplicial resolutions in HTT A.2.9.

proof.text: For a fibrant $RT$ put $Y=\operatorname{Hom}(A^\bullet,RT)$ and $X=\operatorname{Hom}(E^\bullet,RT)$ and let $p:X\to Y$ be restriction. They represent the stipulated derived mapping spaces. To check the fibration assertion, let $V(K)$ be the arrow $A^\bullet\otimes_\Delta K\to E^\bullet\otimes_\Delta K$, where the tensor is the coend of copies indexed by the simplices of $K$. It preserves colimits. The coend of $\Delta^n$ is $X^n$: send the copy of $X^r$ indexed by $\alpha:[r]\to[n]$ via $X(\alpha)$, with inverse the copy indexed by the identity. For the boundary each $\alpha$ factors through a proper injective face, and the coend relations identify its surjective factor, giving $L_nX^\bullet$. Thus $V(\partial\Delta^n)\to V(\Delta^n)$ is a cofibration in the direct arrow model: its source component is $L_nA^\bullet\to A^n$ and its corner component is $A^n\amalg_{L_nA^\bullet}L_nE^\bullet\to E^n$. The collapse maps $V(\Delta^n)\to V(\Delta^0)$ are objectwise weak equivalences, since their composites with the augmentations are weak equivalences. The boundary-collapse theorem in this arrow model makes $V(\Lambda_k^n)\to V(\Delta^n)$ a trivial cofibration. Its corner $A^n\amalg_{A^\bullet\otimes_\Delta\Lambda_k^n}(E^\bullet\otimes_\Delta\Lambda_k^n)\to E^n$ is consequently a trivial cofibration in $\mathrm{sCat}$. By the coend adjunction, a horn-lifting problem for $p$ is exactly a lifting problem from this corner against $RT\to1$, which has a solution. Thus $p$ is a Kan fibration.

source.place: Agent relative-frame horn calculation; uses the coend form of the boundary-collapse criterion, not a simplicial enrichment of the Bergner model category.

proof.text: The comparison $\pi_0Y\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(A,T)$ identifies homotopic vertices with the same induced functor $\pi_0A\to\pi_0RT$ up to natural isomorphism. Naturality conjugates the distinguished arrow by endpoint isomorphisms, and conjugation preserves invertibility. Hence the subset of invertible-arrow vertices is a union of components, namely $E_T$. A vertex of $X$ is a functor $E\to RT$; it sends the invertible class of $j(a)$ to an invertible class. Every simplex has all its vertices in a single component, so $p$ factors through $E_T$.

source.place: HTT A.3.5.3, necessity; representative independence from the natural pi_0 comparison and elementary conjugation.

proof.text: Let $f:A\to RT$ represent an invertible-arrow vertex of $Y$. Apply the inverse-adjunction pushout lemma with $C=RT$ and this exact $f$. The canonical inclusion $b:RT\to RT\amalg_A E$ is a trivial cofibration. In the square with top map $1_{RT}$ and right map the fibration $RT\to1$, a lift gives a retraction $h:RT\amalg_A E\to RT$ with $hb=1$. The restriction $E\to RT$ of $h$ extends $f$ exactly and hence is a vertex of $X$ above $f$. Thus $X\to E_T$ is surjective on vertices. This argument allows the two endpoints of $f$ to coincide.

source.place: HTT Remark A.3.2.15 and Lemma A.3.5.3: trivial-cofibration retraction argument, with the invertibility hypothesis explicit.

proof.text:
Form $P=E\amalg_A E$. Both legs of this span are the cofibration $j$, and all three objects are cofibrant, so $P$ is a homotopy pushout under the conventions of the derived-pushout node. Apply the inverse-adjunction lemma with $C=E$ and $f=j$, whose distinguished class is invertible by step 1. The first inclusion $u:E\to P$ is a weak equivalence. The fold $v:P\to E$ satisfies $vu=1_E$, so it too is a weak equivalence. Homotopy invariance and the natural restriction comparison give weak equivalences
$$\operatorname{Map}^h(E,T)\xrightarrow{v^*}\operatorname{Map}^h(P,T)\simeq X\times_Y^h X.$$
The composites with both projections are the identity, since the fold restricts to the identity on both copies. By compatibility of the comparison with maps of spans, their composite is the homotopy diagonal of $p$.

source.place: Agent strengthening of the double-inversion cylinder argument in HTT Proposition A.3.5.5 to full function complexes.

proof.text: Since $p$ is a Kan fibration, the path comparison $k:X\times_Y X\to X\times_Y^h X$ is a weak equivalence. Its composite with the ordinary diagonal $d:X\to X\times_Y X$ is the homotopy diagonal of step 6, so $d$ is a weak equivalence by two-out-of-three. The first projection $\operatorname{pr}_1:X\times_Y X\to X$ is a Kan fibration, being a pullback of $p$, and $\operatorname{pr}_1d=1_X$. It is therefore a weak equivalence and a trivial Kan fibration. For any vertex $x$ of $X$, pulling this trivial fibration back to $x$ gives $p^{-1}(p(x))\to\Delta^0$ as a trivial Kan fibration. In particular every nonempty vertex fiber of $p$ is weakly contractible. These pullback assertions follow directly from the right lifting characterizations of fibrations and trivial fibrations: a square over a pullback composes to a square for the original map and its lift pairs with the fixed base map.

source.place: Agent diagonal-to-fiber argument; path comparison for a Kan fibration and the Kan model lifting characterizations.

proof.text: The union $E_T$ of components of the Kan complex $Y$ is Kan: a horn with all vertices in those components has every filler in the same components. The factor $p_E:X\to E_T$ is also a Kan fibration, since any lift for its composite with $E_T\hookrightarrow Y$ remains a lift over $E_T$. By step 5, every vertex $y$ of $E_T$ equals $p(x)$ for some $x$; step 7 makes its fiber contractible. The Kan-fibration fiber criterion now makes $p_E$ a weak equivalence and a trivial Kan fibration. A vertex outside $E_T$ has empty strict fiber by step 4. Strict fibers represent homotopy fibers for this fibration by the path comparison. Thus the required homotopy fibers are contractible on $E_T$ and empty outside it. This also covers $T=\varnothing$, where $X=Y=E_T=\varnothing$.

source.place: Agent completion using the Kan-fibration fiber criterion; no identification from pi_0 alone.

proof.text: For an enriched functor $T\to T'$, the induced functor on path-component categories sends isomorphisms to isomorphisms. Hence restriction comparisons preserve the selected unions of components. Use the natural replacement/frame comparisons of the derived-pushout node to compare any stipulated function-complex models with $X\to Y$. They commute with restriction up to the specified comparison homotopies, and their bijections on components preserve the invertibility condition by the induced-functor clause. Therefore they restrict to weak equivalences on $E_T$ and carry the factorization and its equivalence to the arbitrary models in the statement. Homotopy fibers are unchanged under these comparisons by homotopy-pullback invariance. The explicit relative frames of steps 2-3 give the promised compatible choices with $A^0=A$ and a Kan fibration. No saturation assumption or strict inverse choice entered any step.

source.place: Agent naturality and change-of-function-complex-model argument using the stipulated natural comparisons.

tool_uses.why: Constructs the relative cosimplicial frames with degree zero prescribed; the biduality unit has no arbitrary-model diagram theorem.
Converts relative-frame latching cofibrations and augmentation equivalences into the horn lifting condition without assuming simplicial enrichment.
Provides the Kan and trivial-fibration lifting characterizations used for relative frames and pullback stability.
Identifies the strict pullback of the framed restriction fibration with its homotopy pullback and similarly identifies its fibers.
Concludes that the surjective framed fibration with contractible vertex fibers is a weak equivalence.
Makes the homotopy-fiber assertion invariant under the stipulated natural weak equivalences of function-complex models.

HTT is not in literature/, so I fetched the public PDF and read pp. 861-863 and 891-893. The new node lem-coef-simplicial-invertible-arrow-pushout is exactly Remark A.3.2.14 (*') for sSet (Example A.3.2.18, Dwyer-Kan): arbitrary C, no cofibration condition on f, and pi_0 invertibility is the same as invertibility in hC. Its cofibration clause is cobase change of j. It is not a duplicate of inversion-universal-property, cofibrant-simplicial-inversion or cofibrant-homotopy-groupoid-completion, and it does not restate a clause of the item. Step checks: step 1 builds [1] from the I-generators and uses that an equivalence reflects isomorphisms. Step 2 builds the arrow-category Reedy frames with the degree-zero prescription. Step 3 obtains the horn lift from the boundary-collapse test in Arr(sCat); the collapse is a weak equivalence because the degree-zero augmentation is the identity. Step 4 shows the union of components is well defined. Step 5 is the retraction of HTT Lemma A.3.5.3. Step 6 uses the double pushout of A.3.5.5, whose span hypothesis holds. Step 7 goes from the diagonal to contractible fibers via the path comparison. Step 8 applies the fiber criterion and covers T empty. Step 9 is naturality. Edge cases tested: T empty, a noninvertible arrow, a one-object group, coincident endpoints. No cycle (DFS run), every cited id exists, uses equal proof_deps.
